findings.reason: The variant is printed small and unpointed. The candidate's own note says it added the pointing on הַיּוֹם. Remove the added vowels and keep the variant as printed. The marker letter is a separate open question; see the uncertainties.

The vav of the shortened response cue on this line has the same vertical two-dot sheva below it as the וְ״מַ cues on the other lines. There is no shuruk dot inside the vav. The gershayim do come after the מ, as the candidate has them. The print sets the cue tight against שֶׁהָיָה, and the parenthetical touches the words on both sides, but this is typesetting spacing. The candidate's spacing is acceptable.

uncertainties.question: In all three places, the second letter of the small superscript role mark is broad and looks more like ר (קר״ח) than ה, and the left leg of ה cannot be seen. Is it קה״ח, or another letter such as קו״ח (קהל וחזן)? Check all three places the same way, because this will become a role description.

The first word of the rubric is in Rashi script. As printed, the glyphs look like נפפר״ם. Is the Rashi reading בספר״ם, and is the last letter ם or ס? Rashi final mem and samekh look alike here: the ם at the end of 'אומרים' in the same line looks like ס. The expansion of the abbreviation is unknown, and the English page has no translation of this rubric to help.

There are four small Rashi-script variant markers: before גֵּעַשׁ, סוּרוּ מִנִּי, כערכך, and היום. All four use the same glyph. The candidate reads נ״א on s246 and כ״א on s248, which is inconsistent. The glyph looks like כ״ח, which fits Rashi נ״א (nusach acher). Decide on one reading and use it in all four places.

Under the yod there is a three-dot triangle, which looks like segol, together with a meteg. Is the print יֶֽרְשׁוּ (segol), or hiriq plus meteg with a stray dot? I did not substitute the expected יִרְשׁוּ from memory.
There is a hyphen-like mark at mid-height between בחוניו and לפארו. It sits too low for a maqaf, so I take it as a print artifact. Please confirm before dropping it.
The mark under the mem of מגיד (after מוּל) looks like a T-shaped qamats rather than a patah. Is the print מָגִּיד?
Is the mark under the ע a plain sheva or a hataf patah (וּמַעֲלִים)?
